page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-960s-amd is an AMD EPYC-powered virtual server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 960 GB local NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI.

Benchmarks reveal top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 10%. Memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks and single-threaded compression tasks perform strongly in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded decompression and database operations show weaker performance, landing in the bottom 25%. Large-model inference is highly constrained, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high memory and NVMe storage capacity relative to its 4-vCPU compute footprint, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound tasks that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, caching layers, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications. It is less optimal for highly parallelized database operations or heavy language model inference.
